solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scowl when sailor enters that party

indicators.note: the sailor goes into the middle of the word for scowl, so enters marks a container

parts.note: to lour (or lower) is to scowl or look sullen
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A grumpy look crosses someone's face as a sailor walks into a party.
explanation.walkthrough: LABOUR is the British Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is one of the main British political parties, so the name stands for a party.

clue.text: Friendly Lib Dem's question of self-doubt?

parts.note: 'am I?' is a question showing self-doubt
Vince Cable was a leading Liberal Democrat politician

explanation.surface: A friendly Liberal Democrat wonders whether he is really himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as AM I CABLE?, the doubting question of Vince Cable, a Liberal Democrat leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly and good-natured, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Not required — too plain, to put it horribly

indicators.note: putting the words horribly means arranging their letters badly

explanation.surface: Something is optional, or put bluntly, far too plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional is left to choice, so it is not compulsory.

clue.text: Withdrew to be given therapy again?

definitions.meaning: pulled back or retired from a position
read as ..., given medical treatment a second time

explanation.definitionFit: Retreated means withdrew, and split as re-treated it means given treatment once more.

clue.text: Fair cut taken by graduate

indicators.note: the cut is taken by the graduate, so the graduate's letters come first

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
lanced means cut, as a boil is lanced

explanation.surface: A fair share of the cuts is taken by a university graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: A balanced, even-handed judgement is a fair one; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Philosopher errs, last blunder being awful

indicators.note: being awful suggests the letters are a mess needing rearrangement

explanation.surface: A thinker keeps making mistakes, his latest blunder dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher and logician.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertrand Russell was a celebrated twentieth-century British philosopher.

clue.text: Film gallery to the south of a church

indicators.note: in a down clue the gallery sits below, south of, the earlier letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A film showing a gallery to the south of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie but is a material.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is a plastic sheet material used as photographic or overhead-projector film.

clue.text: Quickly providing meat for two?

definitions.meaning: two cuts of meat, one chop and another chop

explanation.definitionFit: Chop-chop is an exclamation urging speed, meaning quickly, and literally two chops.

clue.text: Verdict that's right for Conservative brings jeers

indicators.note: right for Conservative means the letter for right replaces the one for Conservative

parts.note: a decision is a verdict

explanation.surface: A ruling that swaps a right-winger for a Tory draws boos.
explanation.walkthrough: C in DECISION becomes R. 'jeers' is a plural noun standing for mockery as a mass noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Derision is mockery and scorn, as expressed by jeers.

clue.text: Supremo who may have words for his PA?

definitions.text: who may have words for his PA?
definitions.meaning: a boss who reads out letters for a personal assistant to take down

explanation.definitionFit: A dictator is an absolute ruler, and also someone who dictates words for a secretary to write.

clue.text: Swallow seen in SW county mostly and old city

indicators.note: mostly means the county name loses its last letter

parts.note: Devon is a county in south-west England
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A swallow spotted in Devon and in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England, and 'mostly' trims its end. 'Swallow' looks like the bird but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To devour is to swallow food greedily, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Abort use possibly? One might well do that

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to abort a use, as a wrecker might.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ABORT USE gives the answer, and a wrecker might well abort things.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately wrecks plans, and making something abort is just what such a wrecker does.

clue.text: Social occasions about to be restricted by Europeans

indicators.note: the word for about is held in by the Europeans, so it sits inside

parts.note: Danes are Europeans from Denmark
C, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Social events are about to be curbed by European authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: Dances are parties with dancing, a kind of social occasion.

clue.text: Worker and English girl taken aback — they can sense things

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect

indicators.note: taken aback, read literally, means the girl's name is taken backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An employee and an English girl are startled, as if they had sensed something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns the girl's name round; the English letter comes last although the clue names it first, and 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Antennae are the feelers insects use to sense their surroundings.

clue.text: Fish bar so fancied up with lace

indicators.note: fancied up suggests the letters are dressed into a new form

explanation.surface: A fish bar is decorated with lace trimmings.
explanation.definitionFit: The albacore is a long-finned tuna, an ocean fish.

clue.text: Alarm a beautiful woman on the phone

indicators.note: heard over the phone, the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: An alarm goes off as a beautiful woman talks on the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell is rung as an alarm or warning, as with a fire bell.

clue.text: Bit of ship to buckle on trips at sea

parts.note: to bow is to bend or buckle

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of trips are jumbled

explanation.surface: A piece of a ship buckles during sea voyages.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowsprit is the spar projecting from a ship's bow, so part of a ship.

clue.text: Our solid change, just one old coin

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters

explanation.surface: Our solid change amounts to just one old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The louis d'or was a gold coin of pre-revolutionary France.

clue.text: Spread with endless wallop

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to spank is to wallop or smack

explanation.surface: Spread something with a hearty wallop.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the spread or extent of something, as of wings.

clue.text: Bleakness always bearing down on one in hovel

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the hovel

parts.note: a sty is a filthy hovel

indicators.note: in a down clue, bearing down on means sitting on top of

parts.note: ever means always
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Grimness forever weighs on someone living in a slum.
explanation.definitionFit: Severity can mean harshness or austerity, the bleakness of a stark scene.

clue.text: Sort of composer, a m-man working in the countryside?

parts.note: a ranger works in the countryside, and the stammer of m-man repeats the first letter

explanation.surface: A kind of musician stammers about a man who works outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'm-man' signals a stutter, so RANGER becomes R-RANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An arranger adapts music for performance, a type of composer.

clue.text: Lovely party limited by a half-hearted host with no manners

indicators.note: the party is hemmed in by the letters around it, so it sits inside
half-hearted means one of the two middle letters goes

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly crowd, a host behaving badly
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A lovely party is spoiled by an unenthusiastic, ill-mannered host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of the doubled middle letters. 'host' looks like the party-giver but means a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means delightful or lovely, an everyday synonym.

clue.text: Draw a short time, having got paper

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a tract is a pamphlet or paper

explanation.surface: Drawing for a brief while once a paper has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw in, as a magnet draws metal.

clue.text: Good folk are not vulgar in the middle of lesson

indicators.note: in places the slang word inside the middle letters
the middle of picks out the central pair of letters of lesson

parts.note: ain't is a vulgar, nonstandard form of are not

explanation.surface: Decent people aren't rude in the middle of a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: AIN'T is the nonstandard contraction of are not, hence 'vulgar'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints are holy, virtuous people, so good folk in a loose sense.

clue.text: A lie Scot put out about the community

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scot is annoyed by a lie told about his community.
explanation.definitionFit: Societal means relating to society, that is concerning the community.

clue.text: A maths unit that's little short of brilliant

indicators.note: little short of means the word lacks just its final letter

parts.note: radiant means shining, brilliant

explanation.surface: A mathematical unit that is very nearly brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little short of' drops the T of RADIANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The radian is the standard unit of angle in mathematics.

clue.text: Money coming in from grannies working

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are set to work in a different order

explanation.surface: Income earned by grandmothers who still have jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are income, the money that comes in from work.

clue.text: Performance with story that must be listened to? Run away

parts.note: a turn is a stage act or performance

indicators.note: a story listened to is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A show with a narrative you must hear; then flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is an idiom meaning to run away or flee.

clue.text: Female author speaks about Buckingham Palace hostess

indicators.note: speaks goes about, around, the hostess's letters

parts.note: says means speaks
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, who hosted at Buckingham Palace

explanation.surface: A woman writer talks about the hostess at Buckingham Palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy L. Sayers was an English crime writer; Buckingham Palace is the monarch's London home.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy L. Sayers, creator of Lord Peter Wimsey, was a female author of detective novels.
